newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland picks HSBC group as PBK sale adviser. [CORRECTED 16:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland picks HSBC group as PBK sale adviser. [CORRECTED 16:27 GMT]

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry said in a statement that it had picked a consortium led by the HSBC Investment Services Sp. z o.o. as its adviser in the privatisation of the state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK).
The other members of the group include: HSBC Investment Bank Ltd, Arthur Andersen Ltd, Amhurst (corrects from Arnhurst) Brown Sp z.o.o, NBS Sp z.o.o. and BRE bank's brokerage house.
PBK, one of nine state-owned commercial banks spun off the central bank in 1989, is slated for sale in April 1997. It will be the fifth of the nine to be privatised.
Andrzej Chmiel, the head of the selection commission, said the treasury would pay HSBC 5.7 million zlotys plus as "success fee" linked to the value of sold shares.
"The commission decided that the HSBC offer best fit the requirements of tender...including among others its ability to meet its obligations by the end of April 1997," Chmiel told Reuters.
The commission said in its official statement the success fee would be set at 0.675-0.725 percent of the value of the sold shares and would amount to a maximum of 12.2-13.1 million zlotys.
In 1995 PBK bank had a capital of 527 million zlotys and a balance sheet total of 6.8 billion zlotys.
The finance ministry has signalled that it wants to offer about 65 percent of the bank to a strategic investor or a group of investors.
